Your newborn can't taste salt — at all 🤯

Your newborn can't taste salt — at all 🤯

Babies are born with working taste receptors for sweet, bitter, sour, and umami. But not salt.

Salt-detecting taste receptors don't activate until around 4 months of age. Before that, a newborn literally cannot register salty flavor.

The likely reason: breast milk is sweet, not salty. Evolution had no reason to wire salt detection in at birth.

At 4 months, the switch flips — and many babies immediately show a preference for salty foods.

Your newborn has no immune system of their own — yet 🛡️ At birth, babies rely entirely on maternal antibodies passed through the placenta and breast milk. This borrowed immunity protects against most infections for about 6 months. Then it fades — and babies must build their own immune defenses from scratch. This is exactly why the vaccine schedule is timed the way it is. The first shots are calibrated to the window before borrowed immunity disappears. Six months of protection. Then they're on their own. #babyfacts #newborn #immunesystem #vaccines #breastfeeding #maternalimmunity #infanthealth #parenting

Your baby's eye color isn't real yet 👀 Most newborns are born with blue-gray or dark gray eyes — regardless of their genetics. The reason: melanocytes (the cells that produce pigment) haven't ramped up production yet. They need light exposure to activate. Over the first 6-12 months, melanin builds up — and true eye color emerges. Dark brown eyes = more melanin. Green or hazel = moderate melanin. Blue eyes = low melanin. The eyes you see at birth are a placeholder. #babyfacts #eyecolor #newborn #genetics #infantdevelopment #melanin #babyscience #parenting

Your baby's eye color isn't real yet 👀

Most newborns are born with blue-gray or dark gray eyes — regardless of their genetics.

The reason: melanocytes (the cells that produce pigment) haven't ramped up production yet. They need light exposure to activate.

Over the first 6-12 months, melanin builds up — and true eye color emerges.

Dark brown eyes = more melanin. Green or hazel = moderate melanin. Blue eyes = low melanin.

The eyes you see at birth are a placeholder.
